---
title: "plot_slopes"
format: html
---

A geographic map of slope values.
This expects the parameterRateOfChange `.csv` files generated by the parameterRateOfChange quartobatch to be in `data/exports/parameterRateOfChange/`.
The latest version of these files produced by that workflow can be downloaded from [this gdrive folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1paXYRvTTS1qo2zv5durS0jMRxMCu9kus?usp=drive_link).


## load data
```{R, load data}
library(here)
library(glue)
# parameter_to_plot <- "Nitrate (NO3)"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Phosphate, Filtered (PO4)"
parameter_to_plot <- "Total Nitrogen"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Chlorophyll a, Corrected for Pheophytin"
df <- read.csv(here(glue("data/exports/parameterRateOfChange/{parameter_to_plot}.csv")))
```


## exclude data points on land
```{R}
library(sf)
library(maps)

# 1. Filter out rows with missing coordinates to prevent spatial conversion errors
df_valid <- df[!is.na(df$OriginalLongitude) & !is.na(df$OriginalLatitude), ]

# 2. Convert the dataframe into a spatial sf object
df_sf <- st_as_sf(df_valid, coords = c("OriginalLongitude", "OriginalLatitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# 3. Retrieve the Florida land boundary polygon
# (Since SEACAR projects focus on Florida coastal waters, we check against the Florida state boundary)
fl_map <- map("state", region = "florida", fill = TRUE, plot = FALSE)
fl_sf <- st_as_sf(fl_map) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326)

# 4. Check for intersection between the coordinate points and the land polygon
on_land <- st_intersects(df_sf, fl_sf, sparse = FALSE)

# 5. Retain only points that do NOT fall on the land polygon
df_clean <- df_valid[!rowSums(on_land) > 0, ]

message(paste("Removed", nrow(df) - nrow(df_clean), "points located on land."))

# Override the main dataset with the marine-only dataset
df <- df_clean
```


## load helper functions and common packages
```{R}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(h3jsr)

# Updated helper function to accept a target column variable to aggregate
make_hex_layer <- function(df, res, var_name = "significant_slope") {
  agg <- df |>
    mutate(h3 = point_to_cell(
      cbind(OriginalLongitude, OriginalLatitude),
      res = res
    )) |>
    group_by(h3) |>
    # Dynamically average the column specified in var_name
    summarise(avg_value = mean(.data[[var_name]], na.rm = TRUE),
              n         = n(), .groups = "drop")
  polys <- cell_to_polygon(agg$h3)
  st_sf(agg, geometry = polys, crs = 4326)
}
```


## create static hexagon map with coordinates
```{R}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggspatial)

# === SET THE VARIABLE YOU WANT TO MAP ===
# Options: "significant_slope", "coefficient.of.variation", "mean"
target_variable <- "mean" 

# Filter for finite values of our chosen variable
df_static <- df %>% filter(is.finite(.data[[target_variable]]))

# 1. Aggregate points into static H3 hexagons
static_res <- 6
hexsf_static <- make_hex_layer(df_static, res = static_res, var_name = target_variable)

# 2. Extract valid non-NA values to calculate scale bounds
valid_vals <- hexsf_static$avg_value[is.finite(hexsf_static$avg_value)]

# 3. Build map base
p <- ggplot(hexsf_static) +
  # Light background map tile
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoom = 8) + 
  # Render the H3 Hexagons using geom_sf
  geom_sf(aes(fill = avg_value), color = "#ffffff", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.8)

# 4. Apply scale options dynamically based on the target variable
if (target_variable %in% c("mean")) {
  # LOG SCALE scale options for positive-only physical concentration values
  # Filter out any non-positive values to prevent log transformations of <= 0
  positive_vals <- valid_vals[valid_vals > 0]
  color_limits <- c(min(positive_vals, na.rm = TRUE), max(positive_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
  
  p <- p + scale_fill_viridis_c(
    trans = "log10",                
    limits = color_limits,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = paste("Avg", target_variable, "\n(Log10 Scale)")
  )
} else if (target_variable == "significant_slope") {
  # Symmetric bounds and diverging palette for trends/slopes
  quantile_bound <- max(abs(c(
    quantile(valid_vals, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 
    quantile(valid_vals, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  )))
  color_limits <- c(-quantile_bound, quantile_bound)
  
  p : p + scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "BrBG", 
    limits = color_limits,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Avg Significant\nSlope"
  )
} else {
  # Sequential limits and palette for positive-only variance metrics (CV)
  color_limits <- c(0, max(valid_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
  
  p <- p + scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "YlOrRd", 
    limits = color_limits,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Avg Coefficient\nof Variation"
  )
}

# 5. Add spatial context and render the final plot
p +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.5) +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326,
           xlim = range(df_static$OriginalLongitude, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-0.2, 0.2),
           ylim = range(df_static$OriginalLatitude, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-0.2, 0.2)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste(gsub("\\.", " ", target_variable), "in", parameter_to_plot),
       subtitle = paste("Static representation using H3 Hexagons (Res ", static_res, ")", sep=""),
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

```
